column1: # The family runs (store/family_runs/known-2026-10-29.tsv) the Rust host refuses on two vCPUs, held there by name to the refusal (Sprint 351): family, run, the stop w2m-vm --vcpus 2 writes. One refusal: a run that starts a child process, refused until the Machine has its own thread, the run-loop design's card 4f (crates/w2m_vm/src/host_request.rs MACHINE_ON_ONE; Sprint 325). Until Sprint 360 a second: a run whose family starts on the instruction clock, refused before any VM (crates/w2m_vm/src/run.rs vcpus_allowed; Sprint 315); from Sprint 360 that clock stays on one vCPU and a family's start on it runs on the wall clock above one (w2m-vm), and the two processes runs it held start a child process, so they were held to MACHINE_ON_ONE. From Sprint 364 (card 4f3 of docs/design-a-process-that-starts-another-2026-11-26.md) the refusal of a child process is gone: a process that starts another runs on two vCPUs, its child on one, what crosses between them answered by the request server, and the six runs held here (process_parameters 38194049597 and 38194051809, processes 38189162864 and 38189164581, time_and_error_mode 38206225386 and 38206227300) are held to their one-vCPU runs' rows. The list holds none. Held by crates/w2m_vm/tests/family_runs.rs, which fails a run listed here, and a run not listed here that stops otherwise than on one vCPU
